intro: から marks where something starts and まで where it stops: picture a line drawn from one point to another, with the action filling the whole line. までに is different: it is a wall at the end of the line, a deadline. The action happens once, at any point before the wall, and is then finished.

skills.rule: If the action or state lasts all the way up to the point ("until"), use まで; if it happens once, at some time no later than the point ("by"), use までに.
skills.explain:
Ask these questions in order.

1. Is it a place? Places take まで only: 駅まで歩きました. までに is for time.

2. Does the verb describe something that goes on through the period: 待つ, 働く, 寝る, いる, 降る, 勉強する, 開いている? Use まで: 五時まで働きます.

3. Is it a single act that is then done: 出す, 返す, 終わる, 帰る, 着く, 決める, 払う? Use までに: 五時までに帰ります.

Both work after a verb in dictionary form: 母が帰るまで待つ (wait until she returns) and 母が帰るまでに掃除する (clean before she gets back). The same verb can go either way, so check what fills the time.

The English test works: "until" is まで, "by" is までに. That covers negatives too: "I won't know until Friday" is 金曜日まで分かりません, because the not-knowing lasts until Friday. までに includes the deadline itself; for "before" in the sense of earlier than, use 前に.
patterns: [verb dictionary form] まで / までに
A から B まで  "from A to B"

examples.jp: 毎日[まいにち]五時[ごじ]{まで}働[はたら]きます。
examples.en: I work until five every day.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は五時[ごじ]{までに}帰[かえ]ります。
examples.en: Today I'll be home by five.

examples.jp: 図書館[としょかん]は夜[よる]八時[はちじ]{まで}開[あ]いています。
examples.en: The library is open until eight in the evening.

examples.jp: 金曜日[きんようび]{までに}レポートを出[だ]してください。
examples.en: Please hand in the report by Friday.

examples.jp: 雨[あめ]が止[や]む{まで}ここで待[ま]ちましょう。
examples.en: Let's wait here until the rain stops.

examples.jp: 母[はは]が帰[かえ]る{までに}部屋[へや]を掃除[そうじ]しておきます。
examples.en: I'll have the room cleaned by the time my mother gets home.

contrast.note: The action fills the whole stretch up to the point and stops there. 十時まで勉強した: you were studying the whole time until ten.
A deadline for one action, which can happen at any moment before it. 十時までに宿題を終えた: the homework was done at some point no later than ten.
前に means simply "before" with no deadline sense: 寝る前に歯を磨く. Use までに when there is a limit that must not be passed.

mistakes.bad: 明日[あした]{まで}この本[ほん]を返[かえ]してください。
mistakes.good: 明日[あした]{までに}この本[ほん]を返[かえ]してください。
mistakes.note: Returning a book is one act with a deadline: "by tomorrow" is までに.

mistakes.bad: 友達[ともだち]を六時[ろくじ]{までに}待[ま]ちました。
mistakes.good: 友達[ともだち]を六時[ろくじ]{まで}待[ま]ちました。
mistakes.note: Waiting fills the whole time up to six and is never a one-off act: "until" is まで.

mistakes.bad: 駅[えき]{までに}歩[ある]きました。
mistakes.good: 駅[えき]{まで}歩[ある]きました。
mistakes.note: A place is the end of a route, never a deadline: まで only.

skills.tip: Put "until" and "by" into the English sentence. Whichever fits tells you: until is まで, by is までに.
